The pan-Canadian median wait for community mental health counselling was 25 days: half of people had a first session scheduled within 25 days and half waited longer [1]. CIHI tracks the median number of calendar days clients wait for their first scheduled appointment for ongoing community mental health counselling [3]. Early counselling can improve long-term mental health and prevent hospitalization [2].

**Sources**

A meta-review of systematic reviews found a statistically significant association between obesity and depression in all nine included meta-analyses, with odds ratios from 1.18 to 1.57 (BJPsych Open) [2]. A 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis of Mendelian randomization studies (Obesity Reviews, doi:10.1111/obr.70156) reported evidence that general adiposity is causally associated with depression [2].
